accuracy.evidence: Checked against Development Matters (2021): Expressive Arts and Design 3 and 4 year olds 'remember and sing entire songs', Communication and Language 'sing a large repertoire of songs', Reception 'learn rhymes, poems and songs', and the ELG Being Imaginative and Expressive. Nursery rhyme knowledge at 3 predicting later rhyme and phoneme skills is from Maclean, Bryant and Bradley (1987); naps aiding preschool learning from Kurdziel, Duclos and Spencer (2013). All rhymes used are traditional and public domain. p2, p3, m5 and m7 give whole positive answers at every range corner (p3 min is 4-3=1).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the beliefs that hearing a song once is enough (challenge 'Hear it only once', m1), that a whole song is learned in one go (step 5 prediction 'All four at once', m3), that you need to see or hear every word to say it (step 3 prediction, m9) and that a song known today is known for ever (step 6 prediction 'All of it, for ever', m6). The adult text names each under Common mistakes, plus always singing for the child.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagbyheart is the only lab where a young child practises recall of a song: a star filling with each repetition, rhyme-cued end words, the disappearing-words technique on Twinkle, Twinkle, Incy Wincy actions, line-by-line build-up and three days of singing with overnight fade. flagmem and flagmnem are for ages 8+ and use a memory desk, chunked letters and mnemonics; the 30% shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea is felt by doing it: the star only fills a third per 'Say it together', the next rhyme only appears after the child picks the word that sounds like dock, wall or moon, ten word cards vanish two at a time while the child says the line, the spider only climbs or gets washed down after the matching action, a new line is refused until the child sings from the start, and the bars show 50% then 75% kept after each night.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options a 3 or 4 year old might pick: the mouse ran up the … (Shoe, Bed), 'We hide the words, two at a time. Can you still say the line?' (No, I need to see every word), 'A song has four lines. What is the best way to learn it?' (All four at once, one time) and 'Tomorrow, how much will you know?' (All of it, for ever). Each is answered by the task after it.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The Challenge cycles five questions (what helps learn a song, Humpty Dumpty end word, a song too long, remembering Incy Wincy, what to do tomorrow) and rotates the answer order. Every wrong answer has its own why() line, ten m= messages in all, e.g. 'Sock does not sound like wall. Listen to the end of the line before.' and 'Some of it fades in the night. Sing it again tomorrow to keep it.'

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK grade 0.6 (family target 5.0) in short spoken sentences a grown-up can read aloud, and the adult text 6.3 (target 10.0). Lab prompts are under fifteen words, e.g. 'Learn one line. Sing from the start. Then add the next line.' Curriculum wording is kept exact: remember and sing entire songs, large repertoire, rhymes, poems and songs.

no_filler.evidence: No praise padding or 'let's explore' openers. Kid paragraphs each teach one technique with a real rhyme; the adult paragraphs give the curriculum source, why each trick works, the named mistakes and what each lab step does, and lab feedback always says the reason (dock and clock end the same, some fades overnight) rather than only 'well done'.

mobile.evidence: Walked on iPhone 13 emulation in light and dark: rhyme pictures are about 100 px tiles, action tiles are full-width 56 px rows, every canvas action also has a big button below (Say it together, Hide two words, Climb fingers up, Learn the next line, Go to sleep), word cards shrink text to fit, and Show me completed every task on phone and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop and phone; the canvas aria-label changes with each spoken message, every tap target has a button twin in a labelled 'Lab controls' group, Challenge feedback is a polite live region, sound can be switched off, and the clock hands use fixed dark ink so they show on the cream face in dark mode.
